title: Discount codes in the cart
summary:
## Change Map

- `src/cart/discount.ts`: `applyDiscount` posts a code and the subtotal to `/api/discounts`.
- `src/cart/DiscountForm.tsx`: the form that applies a code, prefilled from `?code=` in the page’s URL.
- `src/cart/Cart.tsx`: shows the discount line and the discounted total.
- `src/cart/total.ts`, `src/cart/types.ts`, `src/api/types.ts`: the discount’s type, response type and arithmetic.
- `src/cart/discount.test.ts`, `src/cart/DiscountForm.test.tsx`: the new tests.

## Summary

The feature cannot work as shipped: the response field is misread behind an `any`, the memoised total ignores the discount, and a refused code shows nothing, which its test does not catch. The code field lacks a label, and the applied note renders the typed code as HTML.
strengths: `discount.test.ts` covers the request shape and a refused code with `rejects`, the right way.
Integer cents all the way: `discountAmount` rounds once, in `total.ts`.
`aria-busy` on the form while the code is checked, and a guard against a double submit.

findings.title: The total never updates: discount is missing from the memo

lines: const { items, status, discount, remove, setDiscount } = useCart()

marks.note: not listed here: the memo keeps the first value, null

findings.problem: `useMemo` recomputes `total` only when `items` change. `discount` is read inside but not listed, so the memo keeps the value it computed with `discount` null: the subtotal.
findings.why: The user applies a code, sees the discount line appear, and the total does not move. The feature looks broken, and the total shown is not the one the discount line implies.
findings.fix: Drop the memo, which saves nothing here: `const total = discounted(subtotal(items), discount)`. Listing `discount` in the dependencies works too.

findings.title: A refused code shows nothing: the failure is swallowed

marks.note: any failure: unknown code, expired code, network
back to the start, no message

findings.problem: When `applyDiscount` rejects, for an unknown or expired code as much as for a network failure, the form goes back to `idle` and shows nothing. `Status` has no failed state.
findings.why: The user types a code, clicks Apply, and the form just resets. They cannot tell a wrong code from a broken page, so they retry or give up.
findings.fix: Add a `failed` status set in the `catch`, with a message under the form (`role="alert"`, as `Cart` does when the cart cannot load) that says the code was refused. Keep the typed code so the user can correct it.

findings.title: `any` hides a typo: `data.percentage` is undefined

lines: export async function applyDiscount(code: string, subtotal: number): Promise<Discount> {

findings.problem: `data` is `any`, so `data.percentage` type-checks, but the response field is `percent`: `DiscountResponse` in `src/api/types.ts` says so, and so do the mocks in the tests. Every discount comes back with `percent: undefined`.
findings.why: The discount line shows `Discount (undefined%)` and the total becomes NaN. The feature cannot work, and nothing says why.
findings.fix: Type the call, `request<DiscountResponse>(…)`, and return `data.percent`: the compiler then refuses `percentage`. Drop the `any`.

findings.title: The discount code field has no label

marks.note: a placeholder is not a name: it goes away as the user types

findings.problem: The code field has no label: only a placeholder, which disappears as soon as the user types and is not announced as the field’s name by every screen reader.
findings.why: A screen reader user lands on an unnamed text field with no clue what it takes. The field is also harder to reach on a phone, with no label to tap. The remove buttons in `Cart` show the project names its controls.
findings.fix: Add `<label htmlFor="discount-code">Discount code</label>` before the input and `id="discount-code"` on it. Keep a placeholder only as an example, such as `SAVE10`.

findings.title: The typed code is rendered as HTML

marks.note: the field’s text, or the link’s ?code=

findings.problem: The note is built as an HTML string around `code` and set through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. `code` is what the user typed, or what a link carried in `?code=` (`codeFromLink`). Whatever it holds becomes markup.
findings.why: A link such as `?code=` runs script in the page of whoever opens it, once a real code is applied… or at once, with a code the server accepts. Stored or reflected, it is injection through the discount field.
findings.fix:
Render the code as text: `

Code {code} applied

`. React escapes it.

findings.title: The refused-code test cannot fail

lines: test('tells the user when the code is refused', async () => {

marks.note: null is defined: passes either way

findings.problem: `queryByText` returns `null` when nothing matches, and `toBeDefined()` passes on `null`. The assertion holds whether or not a message shows, so the test passes today, while the form shows nothing on a refused code.
findings.why: The error path looks covered and is not: the swallowed failure in `DiscountForm` ships green, and so will the next regression there.
findings.fix: Assert the message the form should show: `expect(await screen.findByText(/refused/)).toBeInTheDocument()`. It fails until the form shows one.

findings.title: Discount amount formatted by hand
findings.problem: The discount line formats cents by hand, `−$` and `toFixed(2)`, where `CLAUDE.md` asks for `formatPrice` on every amount shown. The total four lines below uses it, and `discountAmount` in `total.ts` already rounds the cents.
findings.why: The two amounts drift: `formatPrice` groups thousands and follows the currency, this line does not, and the rounding is done twice, differently.
